To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) The effluent of the studied industrial discharge has a toxic effect on reproduction in Daphnia magna and on the benthic community, but the effects are not detectable with a chemical survey.

(1) The effluent was toxic to Daphnia, and the toxicity was mainly due to the high concentrations of calcium, cadmia and chloride; (2) The toxicity of the effluents to Daphnia was underestimated by calculating the sum TU of the individual components, and (3) The effluent toxicity could not be predicted by the sum of TUs.

The effluent of a metal finishing industry, containing high loads of CaCl(2) and CdCl(2) as the major toxicants, caused an increased mortality and a reduced reproductive output of Daphnia, when exposed to sub-lethal concentrations of the effluent.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new approach for the assessment of the toxicity of industrial effluent discharges, based on the combination of a toxicity test, an ecological survey and physical/chemical measurements.
the evaluation of a combination of techniques for the detection of the effects of effluents on aquatic ecosystems.
the development of a method to determine the toxicity of an effluent and to predict the effects of the effluent on an ecosystem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effluent has a negative effect on Daphnia magna reproduction, and that the effluent discharge contributes to the background pollution of the river.
the effluent is toxic to Daphnia, that the discharge is toxic to D. magna, that the effluent contains several toxicants which are toxic to D. Magn
the discharge has an effect on the ecosystem of the river and the effluent is the cause of this effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effluent had no significant impact on the river ecosystem, but that the background pollution was responsible for the poor ecological condition of the river.
a combination of techniques is needed to detect the effects of a discharge on the receiving river.
the toxicity test with Daphnia magna is not suitable to determine the effects of the effluent on the river ecosystem as a whole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of effluent toxicity tests, ambient toxicity tests and ecological surveys is essential for the evaluation of the impact of a discharge.
the effluent toxicity test is a valuable tool in assessing the impact of industrial discharges on aquatic organisms, but should be used in combination with other techniques.
the combination of an efflu-ent toxicity test, an ambience toxicity test and an ecologic survey are essential to determine the impact of a discharge on an ecosystem.
